reading.body:
mem0 commands more than two-thirds of the combined 93,859 stars across these three repositories, signaling that a single project has pulled well ahead of its peers in community adoption for agent memory infrastructure.

All three repositories carry Apache-2.0 licences, are unarchived, and received commits within the ten days before this snapshot was generated. The field is active and none of these projects has been abandoned. The gap between mem0 at 64,462 stars and letta at 24,514 is large; zep, at 4,883, sits in a different tier entirely. Star counts measure developer attention, not production deployment or performance, but a gap this wide is unlikely to be noise.

The connection to compute and power is indirect but real. Agents that maintain persistent memory across sessions shift work from the context window, which must be reprocessed at inference time, to external storage that is read selectively. How well that tradeoff is managed affects how much GPU time a given agent workload consumes. This data does not quantify that effect, and it does not cover retrieval latency, storage architecture, or how these projects handle memory at scale. It records only what is publicly visible on GitHub at one point in time.
